title: Hand a part into a receiving cup that keeps moving, without dropping it in
instruction: Hand the aluminium cylinder over into the blue cup. The cup keeps moving and won't wait for you: move along with it, set the cylinder down inside, and let go only when its base is no more than 2 cm above the cup's floor. Don't drop or toss it in.
context: Parts are often handed to a receiver that doesn't hold still: a coworker's hand reaching in, another robot's gripper or a fixture on a moving axis. Dropping a part into it from height damages the part, and a gripper that doesn't move with the receiver knocks it. Done by: assembly-line workers and machine tenders.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. A bare aluminium cylinder (4 cm diameter, 7 cm tall, 240 g) stands upright on the table, its centre 18 cm in front of the line through the bases and 20.5 cm inside the right arm's base (toward the left arm). A blue plastic open receiving cup (10 x 10 cm inside, 12 x 12 cm outside, 1 cm floor and walls, its rim 2.5 cm above its floor) is carried by a two-axis drive 2 mm above the table, square to the arm bases. Positions are of the cup floor's centre, as (cm in front of the bases' line, cm to the right of the right arm's base). It starts at (30, -8.5), i.e. 8.5 cm inside the right arm's base, and loops without end: to (34, 5.5) in 4 s, stops 0.6 s; to (28, -0.5) in 2.5 s; to (36, 9.5) in 3.5 s, stops 0.8 s; back to (30, -8.5) in 5 s, stops 0.4 s (16.8 s per loop). Each move starts and stops smoothly (cosine velocity profile); peak speeds are 5.3 to 6.0 cm/s.
scoring: A release is the moment a gripper holding the cylinder stops holding it. 1.0 if the cylinder ends resting in the cup (centre inside the walls, base within 1 cm of the floor, moving with the cup to within 1 cm/s for 1 s, no gripper holding it) and its last release was over the cup's inside with its base 2 cm or less above the cup floor and the gripper moving within 3 cm/s of the cup (in each 0.05 s step just before and as the cylinder left the fingers). Otherwise, at the end: 0.5 if it rests in the cup (dropped, tossed or let go while moving differently from the cup); 0.25 if its base was ever 3 cm or more above the table; 0 otherwise.
reset_notes: Stop the cup at its start, empty it, stand the cylinder back on its mark, and start the cup's loop with the trial.
fidelity: The cup follows its path exactly, like a stiff servo axis: the arms can't push or stop it. It is five boxes (floor, four walls, 1 mm apart) moving as one. Grip and release are read every 0.05 s from the finger joints and the gripper's position (forward kinematics). The cylinder has rubber-like friction (1.2/1.0), more than aluminium on plastic.
